questions.stem: Which of the following is not used for the treatment of insulin-induced hypoglycemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Beta Blocker
  • Beta-blockers can mask the symptoms of hypoglycemia, such as a rapid heartbeat and tremor because they block the effects of norepinephrine, which results in a slowing of your heart rate and a reduced tremor. Hunger, irritability, and confusion may be concealed as well.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:288

questions.stem: A patient was diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis, but the treating intern gave only insulin rapidly to lower blood glucose. What complication is expected by this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypokalaemia
  • When insulin therapy is instituted ketosis subsides →K+ is driven back intracellularly leading to dangerous hypokalemia.
  • After 4 hours it is appropriate to add 10–20 mEq/hr KCl to the i.v. fluid
  • Further rate of infusion is guided by serum K+ measurements and ECG.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 291

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes presents to his physician for a follow-up. He complains of recurrent hypoglycemic reactions to his medications. Which of these medications is most likely responsible for this patient's hypoglycemic reactions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glyburide
  • Glyburide (sulfonylurea) can cause hypoglycemia in Diabetes mellitus patients.

questions.stem: The oral diabetic dispensed with a black box warning of increased risk of bladder cancer is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Pioglitazone
  • Preclinical and clinical trial data, and results from an observational study suggest an increased risk of bladder cancer in pioglitazone The observational data further suggest that the risk increases with the duration of use. Do not use in patients with active bladder cancer. Use caution when using in patients with a prior history of bladder cancer.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 300

questions.stem: Which OHA can cause fracture?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pioglitazone
  • Treatment with thiazolidinediones (Pioglitazone)has been associated with an increased risk of bone fracture in women with some studies also showing effects in men.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 300

questions.answerText: Pramlintide can be given in patients with gastroparesis
questions.solutionHtml:
Pramlintide can be given in patients with gastroparesis
  • Pramlintide can be given in patients with gastroparesis is an incorrect statement. As pramlintide is contraindicated in patients with gastroparesis or other disorders of motility.

options.label: C

questions.solutionHtml:
Not useful as monotherapy

questions.stem: Following are GLP-1 receptor agonists except for-
questions.solutionHtml:
Pramlintide

Pramlintide is an Amylin mimetic drug.

  • acts through the amylin receptor in specific regions of the hindbrain
  • amylin receptor reduces glucagon secretion, delays gastric emptying, and fosters a feeling of satiety
  • administered as a subcutaneous injection prior to meals.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 293

questions.stem: Anti-diabetic drug contraindicated in medullary carcinoma thyroid patient is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Hirsutism
  • Usage of Propylthiouracil causes hair loss, not Hirsutism.
  • Antithyroid drugs (carbimazole and propylthiouracil) can, in rare cases, cause diffuse hair loss. It may be very difficult to tell whether the hair loss is due to the effects of the previous overactivity of the thyroid or the anti-thyroid drugs.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, Chapter 47, Page No. 879

questions.stem: What should be the next best drug to add with metformin if an obese patient has uncontrollable diabetes with metformin, patient refuse to take an injection, and family h/o bladder cancer present & also has history of pancreatitis in past and has an allergy to sulfonylureas:
questions.solutionHtml:
Canagliflozin
  • As the patient has refused to take injections and family h/o bladder cancer, and pancreatitis in the past and has an allergy to sulfonylureas.


  • Among the options, Canagliflozin is the best drug to be given to this patient as it can be taken orally and also it will help in weight loss.
